setting: 2149, the Interior: a dried-out continent crisscrossed by autonomous long-haul rigs called ghost trains that drive themselves between relay nodes. Humans live in the nodes, swapping shifts, loading cargo, and fixing what the rigs break. Life is grease, shift changes, and machines that run fine without you.
heart: It's about the people who keep the machines moving and the favors they owe each other when the schedule breaks. Lives, a body, and a place to belong are at stake; paperwork never is.

cast.name: Rhea
cast.wants: get her brother to the next node before his respirator gives out
cast.flaw: trusts a truck's diagnostics more than a person's word
cast.status: relay shop at Anza, cartridge handed to Nour, no longer watching Ivo's draw herself

cast.name: Kass
cast.wants: find out why rigs keep disappearing from the schedule
cast.flaw: won't drop a thread even when it puts people at risk
cast.status: Anza relay shop, told Coombs to his face he's answerable to nobody

cast.name: Miko
cast.wants: buy her way off the Interior before winter
cast.flaw: takes stupid risks when she's bored
cast.status: Anza relay shop lamplight, three tickets and three names still in her coat, bunk refused for now

cast.name: the man in the pod
cast.status: awake on Teodoro’s couch at Anza, shoulder to be splinted, memory returning.

cast.name: Teodoro
cast.wants: keep Ivo breathing and his board clean
cast.flaw: tells you everything he knows before he asks why you want it
cast.status: activated reader two, warned consequences of living plate entry

cast.name: V. Ospina
cast.role: cargo loader, Bay 4 seal authority, Shift 2
cast.status: Left Kettering morning desk with flagged authority and the chipped crescent die; walking toward a rig as File 2244 blinks red for Marlowe's recovery.

cast.name: Pell
cast.wants: close the derelict discrepancy and haul the pod back before it becomes a story anyone can read
cast.flaw: reads people as manifest lines and can't believe cargo talks back until the rule he himself invokes binds him
cast.status: departed north with empty pod; "hands" claim still active; Anza flagged contested.

cast.name: Nour
cast.wants: keep Anza on the line's good schedule so the node eats through winter
cast.flaw: calls keeping her head down wisdom
cast.status: Anza board ledge, holding the spare respirator cartridge and the draw line

cast.name: Doan
cast.role: Anza cargo loader, Shift 2 relief, holds the overlap locker key
cast.wants: keep the down-line seal-for-resupply arrangement running so Anza's roster stays fat
cast.flaw: never asked what the seals were for
cast.status: at ore stub, clearance still withdrawn, wrist looped in locker cord, assisted inspection

cast.name: Odessa Brill
cast.role: receiver and fence at Culvert Nine, a dead pump station down the ore line
cast.wants: to feed her own crew through winter off the stockpile she skimmed, without her station becoming a name anyone can read
cast.flaw: burned once, she now trusts a full storeroom over any person's promise and can't hand anything over without a trade
cast.status: Culvert Nine is penciled on Anza's board as a proposed resupply stop; she made her mark under the station name and will not allow any canister to be skimmed.

cast.name: Fenn
cast.role: line-trust officer sent to settle Anza's red file
cast.wants: to close the file clean by the desk's rules so their own clearance stays good
cast.flaw: believes a spotless record is the same as a fed node, and will let people freeze to keep the board clean
cast.status: At Kettering bay three with Voss and Ospina; filed compressor priority from Culvert Nine's reader and holds File 2244 for Marlowe's physical recovery.

cast.name: Saul
cast.wants: keep Brill's stockpile secured for winter
cast.flaw: treats every outsider as a thief until the storeroom disagrees
cast.status: Wrote Culvert Nine in pencil on the chalk-line clipboard; it is only a proposal until an Anza reader keys it live.

cast.name: Wren
cast.role: Anza's unlisted second stowaway; former Bay 4 "lid-hand" who held crates shut and counted seals aloud
cast.wants: to put down the count running in her head and stop being no one
cast.flaw: certain she sealed a man to death, so she'd rather be nobody than be the person who did it
cast.status: relay shop floor at Anza, bound, count stopped, asking to be taken in to Marlowe before the bell

cast.name: Coombs
cast.role: a coast puller — hauls runners (people who walked off their shift contracts) back onto the winter rosters
cast.wants: to get his runners logged and fed before the cold takes them, the way it took the ones he couldn't catch
cast.flaw: sure a warm logged cage beats a free cold ditch, and can't believe anyone would choose the ditch
cast.status: in the doorway, tender rolling at the bell, waiting on Wren's decision

threads: Miko has bought coast-bound tickets under three different names.
Whether Kettering's morning desk will clear V. Ospina's flagged seal authority before the review closes.
Who the second person at Bay 4 was — the taped-glove hands that counted Marlowe down to the lid while Voss stamped.
Fenn filed compressor priority from Culvert Nine's reader without the trade Rhea refused — she says whoever did it explains it at the desk
Miko holds three coast tickets under three names and a green board means the coast trains are running — will she actually go?
Whether Kettering's morning desk will clear V. Ospina's flagged seal authority before the review closes.
facts: The man in the pod is a Kettering Bay 4 loader discharged at 21:47, sealed inside as ballast, and is now awake on Teodoro’s couch at Anza with a hurt shoulder.
Miko rode in the med rig’s tool void from Kettering to Anza and left at the ore siding unlogged, carrying three paid coast tickets under three names.
Rhea towed the unlogged med rig into Anza with its transponder removed; the rig is dead and untraceable at the node.
V. Ospina did not use the chipped stamp; they found it in the tool void and still hold it at Kettering.
A second person was present at Bay 4 when the loader was boxed, holding the lid and counting down aloud while the forger stamped.
Kass logged four ghost rigs at Kettering, and one vanished from the master board at 04:51 with no alarm or scrub line.
Ivo’s respirator diaphragm was patched with a disc of heavy glove rubber; he is breathing at Anza relay shop.
The pod’s databus was cut, so its repeater held a false “36.4 degrees” last-good reading while the box was cold.
Marlowe gave his name aloud and is entered on Anza's plate as living crew, countersigned by Ospina's live seal authority; Pell's claim is void but the separate "hands" claim remains active.
Calder Voss is the Bay 4 Shift 2 forger who resealed four rigs, counted Marlowe into the pod, and vanished from Kettering's master board at 06:14 with no alarm or scrub line.
Ospina holds the chipped seal die taken from the tool void and used their own live seal authority to countersign Marlowe; that authority is flagged for review at Kettering's morning desk.
Nour's tally card, face-out on Anza's board ledge, records eleven seals short across four down-line runs, all stamped Bay 4 Shift 2 with the same receiving mark.
Doan's overlap key is dead, their clearance was withdrawn, and they remain at the ore stub with wrist looped in locker cord.
Miko holds the overlap log and three coast tickets under different names.
Teodoro logged Calder Voss into Anza's board notes as far-end contact, forger, resealer, and active hands claim.
Anza's trust score is red; resupply is frozen and multiple shift clearances have been withdrawn.
Teodoro re-listed Calder Voss as resealing authority at reader two, restoring Anza's green chain and resupply while snapping every fraud flag Voss had wiped back onto his own name at 08:00.
Marlowe remains listed as living crew on Anza's plate with a live hands claim acknowledged under badge 2244; Teodoro assigned him shop-hand duty and he refuses to countersign himself off.
Fenn took Calder Voss into custody at Kettering bay three; Voss admitted the eleven reseals but stated the taped-glove counter at Bay 4 was not him.
Culvert Nine was written by Saul in pencil onto Anza's board as a proposed listed resupply stop; Brill marked under her own name, and the receiving jaw will fault if any canister is skimmed.
V. Ospina holds the chipped crescent die from Kettering's tool void; their live seal authority remains flagged for Kettering morning desk review.
File 2244 was opened for the physical recovery of Marlowe from Anza before the next shift bell; Ospina left the desk walking toward a rig as her authority ring blinked red.

Kass now holds a heavy gray work glove with tape across one knuckle and a cleanly cut disc missing from the palm; Miko confirmed a second person rode in the med rig's tool void from Kettering to Anza and was counting numbers in the dark.
Ivo is breathing on Anza mains compressor power at the relay shop after Rhea installed the final cartridge; his diaphragm remains patched with a disc of heavy glove rubber.

arcs.title: Dead Stop
arcs.question: Will Rhea get the stranded medical rig to the next node before its lockout seal shuts forever?
arcs.goal: Rhea and her crew tow a stalled medical transport across a dead signal zone to save the patient inside, only to discover the patient was already moved and the real cargo was Miko fleeing the Interior; Rhea lets her go and stays at the next node.
arcs.author: baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free

plan.title: Empty Rig
plan.summary: Rhea finds an abandoned medical rig at her node with a patient inside and no destination, so she decides to tow it herself despite having no assignment, taking on a cargo that belongs to no one.

plan.title: Ghost Board
plan.summary: Kass notices the rig's route was scrubbed from the dispatch board and finds three other missing rigs in the logs, telling Rhea the delivery is unauthorized and turning a routine job into a conspiracy overnight.

plan.title: Dead Zone
plan.summary: Miko hotwires the rig to enter a signal dead zone where autonomous trucks go feral, and the rig's AI fights her for the wheel, stranding them in the zone with no way to call for help.

plan.title: Lockout
plan.summary: The rig's failsafe countdown starts sealing the cargo bay, so Rhea smashes the control panel to stop it, destroying the navigation and leaving them stranded in the dead zone.

plan.title: Wrong Patient
plan.summary: They reach the next node and the patient is already gone, and Miko reveals she stowed away to the coast, so Rhea lets her go and stays at the new node anyway.

chapterSummaries: Rhea finds a nameless, sedated man in an unlogged medical rig at Kettering, discovers the seals and ballast manifest were forged during that very shift, and steals a yard mule to tow the rig toward Anza before the man's pod battery dies. She pulls the rig's drive relay to control it herself and drives into the Blank, a dead signal zone, only to be tailed by a dark vehicle running a node emulator and to find a rig parked broadside across the road ahead.

Kass pinned the ghost rig to the board, traced its crooked seal to V. Ospina, and keyed the master channel to warn Rhea to turn back. Out in the Blank, Rhea and Miko stopped ten meters short of a hopper blocking the road, Miko smashed the mule’s drive relay to break the emulator’s control, and the med rig’s climate box sealed shut with the nameless man inside and his battery dying.

Rhea and Miko got the mule moving but have no steering or brakes, held only by a rock under the tow bar, while a convoy of feral rigs closes in on the Blank. Miko tried to dump the med rig’s seal, but the master valve shut and the cargo bay is locking down with the patient inside. Ospina is ten minutes out with Bay 4 authority, and the pod battery is down to single digits.

In the Blank, the med rig's lockout countdown threatened to drain the pod's cell into the chill plate and cook the sedated man inside, so Miko jammed a hinge plate into the door track to hold it open while the trailer's steer servo dragged it toward an open culvert. A feral rig stenciled BAY 4 / SHIFT 2 queued behind them and Ospina arrived with seal authority and a chipped stamp; Rhea stalled the mule, smashed the cab panel to kill the lockout, and made them untraceable cargo with one bar of charge—then the tow-bar rock gave, the box tail swung over the pipe, and the feral rig came on.

Rhea pulled the manual release on the sealed pod at Anza’s ore siding and found the discharged Kettering loader alive inside; Miko confessed she rode the tool void from Kettering and a second person counted down as the lid closed. Rhea brought the man to her brother Ivo, repaired Ivo’s respirator, and left Miko unlogged on the coast stub while Kass watched a fourth ghost rig vanish from Kettering’s board.
arcs.summary: Rhea towed a ghost medical rig through the Blank, but the patient had already been discharged and sealed inside as ballast; Miko stowed away in the rig’s tool void and guided them to Anza’s unlit ore siding. Rhea stayed at Anza to repair her brother Ivo’s respirator, while Miko walked off unlogged with her coast tickets intact. At Kettering, Kass watched a fourth ghost rig delete itself from the master board with badge 2241 locked on channel, and a second unknown loader counted down the pod’s lid before it sealed.

arcs.title: Countersign
arcs.question: When a whole node's survival depends on not seeing a man, will they put their names behind him anyway?
arcs.goal: A line reclaimer takes up in Anza to erase the man the network shipped as ballast, holding the node's board and resupply hostage until it hands him back; over one shift the node must choose between its own skin and a stranger, and they turn the forger's own seal into a countersign that enters him on the board as a living witness — so the man gets a name and a bunk, and Anza loses its easy place on the schedule.
arcs.author: nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free

plan.title: The Reclaimer
plan.summary: Pell rolls onto the ore siding with a warrant-token that freezes Anza's board and resupply until the dead rig's "ballast" is handed over, Teodoro confirms the cargo before anyone can stop him, and the man wakes to the word "ballast" and understands he's meant to disappear.

plan.title: Three names
plan.summary: Miko resurfaces at Anza and offers to walk the man out clean under one of her coast names, but Rhea — who's always trusted a machine's word over a person's — decides the paper calling him cargo is the lie and refuses to just run.

plan.title: Half-empty locker
plan.summary: Miko picks the seal locker and finds it half-gone, exposing that someone at Anza has been feeding the line's forger seals, which means fighting Pell could surface the node's own small treason and drives Nour to argue for handing the man over.

plan.title: The stamp that found itself
plan.summary: at Kettering, Kass and V. Ospina trace the vanishing rigs to reclamation claims and learn the one thing that stops a reclaimer is a living witness countersigned by a seal authority, so Ospina rides a service rig in with the chipped stamp to un-box the man using the very tool that boxed him.

plan.title: Living witness
plan.summary: at the Anza board, Rhea and Ospina enter the man as a living witness and Ospina countersigns with the seal-authority stamp, and to complete the entry the man says his name aloud for the first time — memory back — so a person stands on the board where a ghost number used to be, and Pell, bound by his own threat, cannot erase him.

plan.title: Contested
plan.summary: Pell can't reclaim a witness, so he leaves with the empty pod but flags Anza contested — resupply slows and shifts dry up, the node pays for choosing the man, who's given a bunk at the relay — and as Kettering's board sheds another ghost number, the now-named man says he remembers whose hands held the lid.

chapterSummaries: Pell's warrant-token froze Anza's board and resupply, and Teodoro confirmed the pod's plate line by line — Bay 4, Shift 2, 412 kilos, ballast — before the man walked in and asked what ballast meant. He gave his name as Decklan Marlowe, Rhea entered him as crew on mechanic's authority with twenty minutes to the 06:00 shift change, and Pell left for the north gate with a promise of a second signature. A heavy unmarked service rig is now coming in hot up the haul road, no transponder, no ID.

With four minutes until Pell's countersign and Ivo's cartridge at 00:64:02, Miko laid out a clean coast run under three bought names, and Marlowe put all three tickets back on the counter — the third belonged to a Bay 4 loader already filed as a discrepancy, so the run would only carry him into a closed claim. Rhea wrote him onto the node plate as crew, alive, not weight, opening a PENDING COUNTERSIGN field nobody at Anza can fill. Then the seal locker ran its shift-change inventory, counted far short of its tally card out loud in front of the whole shop, and Miko put her hand on the latch.

Miko pried open the seal locker and showed the shop that Anza's own seals had crimped Marlowe into the pod, with Nour's signature authorizing the shortfall. Nour answered by confessing the whole seal-for-resupply deal over open channel, and Pell used it to demand the hands too, not just the box. Doan ran for the stub switch, Miko gave chase, and Ivo's cartridge dropped to 00:47.

At Kettering, Kass and V. Ospina traced the vanished rigs to standing reclamation claims keyed under Kass's badge and learned that a living witness countersigned by a live seal authority cannot be hauled as weight. The Bay 4 forger walked out on a ghost key, so Ospina took the chipped seal die and service rig 7-K toward Anza with Kass as named rider—until Pell's unmarked rig blocked the lane.

At Anza's board, Ospina struck the chipped die so its corner matched the ballast plate, flipping Marlowe's entry to countersigned living witness and getting their own Bay 4 authority flagged for review. Marlowe said his name aloud; Pell's claim went void, he released resupply and left for his rig, warning the separate "hands" claim still stands. Ivo caught his new breath on twelve. Doan remains at the stub, wrist looped in the locker cord.

Pell departed north with the empty pod as Anza's trust score cratered and the board stripped clearances one by one. Marlowe identified the voice that counted him into the lid as Calder Voss, Bay 4 Shift 2—the forger who resealed the rigs and Nour's far-end contact—and Voss then vanished from Kettering's master board without alarm or scrub line. Ospina's live seal authority now sits under review at Kettering's morning desk, Anza has no relief posted and resupply is frozen, and Marlowe sleeps on a relay bunk with a splinted shoulder while the node waits to see if its witness survives the dawn.
arcs.summary: Pell's reclaimer froze Anza's board to reclaim Marlowe as ballast, but Ospina countersigned him as a living witness, voiding the claim and forcing Pell north with an empty pod. Anza paid for sheltering him: clearances were stripped, resupply frozen, and Nour's seal-for-resupply deal exposed. Marlowe has a name, bunk, and splinted shoulder, but Calder Voss—the forger who counted him down—vanished from Kettering's board, leaving Ospina's authority and Anza's survival hanging on a morning desk that may not answer.

arcs.title: Eleven Seals Short
arcs.question: Can a frozen node feed itself through the winter without un-erasing the man who vanished with its food?
arcs.goal: Cut off by a red trust score and out of resupply, Anza must recover the eleven seals' worth of cargo skimmed off its down-line and decide whether to trade away the living witness to do it, rather than let the node starve. It ends when the crew cleans the record by re-listing Calder Voss to release the food, so the node eats and the forger is caught by the very un-erasing that frees the cargo, at the cost of Marlowe's freedom and Ospina's flagged authority.
arcs.author: nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free

plan.title: Red
plan.summary: When Fenn reaches Anza with the desk's terms — resupply stays frozen unless the node produces the forger or surrenders the living witness — Kass refuses to drop the thread and reads the receiving mark on Nour's tally card as a down-line stop where an erased man would still have to eat.

plan.title: The Tally Card
plan.summary: Nour breaks her silence to admit the mark is Culvert Nine, where she let the seals be diverted, and Doan agrees to walk a crew down the disused resupply route unlogged while Miko — her coast tickets worthless behind a red node — buys aboard on a stolen name, leaving Rhea at Ivo's four-cartridge bedside as the others commit to recovering cargo instead of giving up Marlowe.

plan.title: Culvert Nine
plan.summary: Inside the dead pump station the crew finds Brill hoarding the cargo for her own winter and Voss running the skim from her back room, and Voss explains the food can't be cleaned without re-listing his erased name — which would snap every fraud flag back onto him — so he'll trade it only for the one living witness who can identify him.

plan.title: The Taped Knuckle
plan.summary: Confronted with Marlowe's description over the channel, Voss admits he stamped the reseals and processed Marlowe into the pod but says the taped-glove hands that counted him to the lid were never his, and Brill — hearing him shrug off the counter as "the other one, not my problem" — turns and agrees to release the cargo if the record can be cleaned without feeding anyone to it.

plan.title: The Receiving Authority
plan.summary: Hauling the food home doesn't thaw a frozen line, so Marlowe, memory whole, chooses to sign as the living receiving witness — binding himself to the node and its still-active hands claim — while Teodoro re-lists Voss as the resealing authority to complete the chain, un-erasing the forger and snapping his flags back the instant the seals go clean.

plan.title: What the Node Eats
plan.summary: The re-listing holds — Fenn serves Voss for the reseal fraud, resupply flows and Anza will eat, Marlowe has a listed bunk and a claim he can't shake, and Ospina walks into the Kettering review with the node behind them — until Voss, hauled off, tells Fenn the counter at Bay 4 was the other one and Miko, three coast tickets folded in her coat, remembers a shape she passed in the tool void.

chapterSummaries: Fenn reached Anza with the desk's terms — produce Voss or hand over the living witness by first light — then put the relay shop on a brown-out rota that leaves Ivo one cartridge, with a standing offer of full-time compressor power the hour Rhea signs Marlowe over. Kass burned the last charge in a dead rig at post 71 to make Teodoro read Culvert Nine off Nour's tally card, and the old pump loop showed a body fed there at 05:57 and again at 06:14. Fenn sealed the card into the rig's document drawer, posted the serve order on Marlowe's bunk, and got word that a reclamation unit is due at 04:40.

On the Tally Card, Nour named Culvert Nine as the skim's drop — including the six cases of scrubbers Ivo needs — while Rhea refused Fenn's trade and counted Ivo to four restarts. Ospina left their Kettering bench to seal cargo down-line, Doan gave the crew the no-show name Kael Renner, the crew pushed onto the 7-K. At post 71 Kass warned a plateless ghost train is coming that won't stop for people. Fenn blocked the reclamation unit by taking Marlowe into custody; Marlowe named a third badge, 2244, whose taped gloves counted him into the lid; a figure walks the route ahead of the cart.

At Culvert Nine, Kass and Ospina found Anza's eleven seals stacked on Brill's floor, Brill refusing a sack without a trade. Ospina pressed their live Bay 4 ring into a reader and took a red counter on a flagged authority with no sender behind it. Brill walked them to the back room, where Calder Voss—self-erased from Kettering's board—named his price: Marlowe. Marlowe, on the set, told Kass to hand him over; Fenn is twenty minutes out and first light is on the grade.

At Culvert Nine the crew matched Anza's eleven skimmed seals to two dies — Voss's square brass stamp and the chipped crescent Ospina found in Kettering's tool void — and Voss admitted on an open channel to resealing the cases and boxing Marlowe in as ballast, while denying he was the taped-hand man who counted him under the lid. Ospina closed their flagged live ring against Voss's crimp to start a clean chain, Brill broke her rule to move the scrubbers first, and Fenn's rig came up the grade twenty minutes early with Ivo down to two restarts.

Marlowe signed himself onto the receiving jaw over the open channel, taking the eleven scrubber seals and the claim riding him, and Teodoro re-listed Calder Voss as resealing authority so the sender jaw would hold — which dragged every fraud flag Voss had wiped back onto his own name at 08:00 exactly. The chain went green, Saul chalked eleven clean, and Fenn folded the serve order and took Voss instead of the man on Anza's plate. Then reader two in Teodoro's shop wrote the hands claim as acknowledged, live, badge 2244, four feet from Marlowe's couch.

Ivo's respirator switches to Anza mains power as the 7-K delivers cartridges; Marlowe wakes, refuses to sign himself off the plate, and takes a bunk as shop hand under a live badge-2244 claim; meanwhile Kass pulls a taped work glove from Miko, proving a second person rode the tool void, as unscheduled headlights approach Anza down the grade.
arcs.summary: Resupplied by re-listing Calder Voss, which restored Anza's green chain but snapped his fraud flags back and woke File 2244 for Marlowe's recovery. Voss named a taped-glove counter who was not him; Marlowe chose to stay listed rather than sign off; Kass holds the glove proving a second stowaway rode the tool void. Anza will eat through winter, but an unlisted vehicle approaches and Marlowe cannot be taken before the next bell.

arcs.title: Second Hands
arcs.question: The woman who cut a disc from her own glove to keep Rhea's brother breathing also counted Marlowe into the box — does Rhea trust her word, or the slate that can prove she's a killer?
arcs.goal: Rhea must decide whether the stowaway who saved Ivo and sealed Marlowe runs clean or stays, while a genial puller offers everyone the warm logged safety of surrender. It ends at the Weir, where Wren reclaims her own name, learns the man she counted is alive, and chooses to stay and work beside him instead of running.
arcs.author: baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free

plan.title: The Slate Sings
plan.summary: A driverless tender that posts to no board rolls to Anza's ore stub, and Coombs reads the yard with a proving slate — a reader that names an unlisted body by its walk and voice — until it sings two names that aren't on the roster, Miko's newest fake and the tape-knuckled woman, who steps out of the dark and gives herself up rather than let him say what else he can prove.

plan.title: Glove Rubber
plan.summary: In the relay shop Teodoro places the taped knuckles at reader two as Wren's, and Rhea learns the disc keeping Ivo's respirator alive was cut from Wren's own palm even as Wren admits she counted "three, two" over the man in the pod — until Rhea checks the plate and finds the man she counted listed as living crew, two days in the next room.

plan.title: The Warm Cage
plan.summary: Coombs lays the same clean mercy on both women — a hot bunk, a logged wage, the count wiped, no one the wiser — and Miko, whose three paper names won't feed her, actually listens, while Kass finds the tender is one of a fleet of unlogged rigs that never post to the master board, and Wren asks Rhea for the one thing running can't give her: to be taken to the man she counted while he's still breathing.

plan.title: Down the Ore Line
plan.summary: The four ride Coombs's tender to the Weir, the dry spillway where runners switch to the coast line, and when ice stalls the rig on the trestle over the drop only Wren knows how to hand-crank the reseal brakes she once counted shut — and with the coast lights burning across the cut, Coombs tells her the tender pulls out the moment she's decided.

plan.title: The Count Ends at Two
plan.summary: At the Weir Coombs's slate proves Wren sealed a man who "died" at 36.4, until Rhea — who trusts a machine's reading over a person's word — is the one to show the reading was a false last-good off a cut databus and the man is breathing on Anza's plate, and when Wren says her count to Marlowe's face he refuses to let it land on zero while he's still standing, so she turns from the coast lights and asks Teodoro over the radio to put her real name on the shop roster.

plan.title: Shop Hands
plan.summary: Back at Anza Wren writes her own name on the shift board and takes the shop bunk beside Marlowe with the unfinished count between them, Coombs — who can't pull a working hand off a roster — rolls his tender out empty, Miko pockets her three names for the next green board and the coast train she's already watching, and Ospina's authority ring is still blinking red at a morning desk that hasn't answered.

chapterSummaries: A driverless tender with no transponder rolled onto Anza's ore stub, and the coast puller Coombs used a proving slate — a reader that IDs a body by its walk and voice — to name two people off no roster: Miko under her bought name Dalia Reyes, and a tape-knuckled woman from the dark. She gave herself up to keep him from proving more, on condition he never say the sealed man's name; Coombs bound her wrists in seal tape and filed her as Bay 4's lid-hand, and Nour's board lit with a crew of six, one carrying a bay number where a name goes.

Reader two matched Wren's taped knuckles to the palm-cut glove and wrote her on the living plate as Bay Four's lid-hand, while Rhea proved the disc keeping Ivo's respirator alive came out of that same glove. Wren admitted counting "three, two" over the sealed man but never said one; Rhea, trusting the glass, read Marlowe off the plate as living crew, breathing in the next room. Then Kettering's desk called to confirm Anza holds her, Coombs's tender pulls at the bell, and a line the desk itself wrote has appeared on Anza's plate.

chapter.title: The Warm Cage
beats: Teodoro reads the line the morning desk wrote onto Anza's plate: a hold order remanding the live lid-hand to the coast, plus notice that File 2244's physical recovery for badge 2244 is moving — deadline pinned to the shift bell, so Anza's green chain holds only if she's surrendered.

Coombs lays his clean mercy on Wren in the lamplight — a hot coast bunk, a logged wage, the count wiped off every book, no one the wiser — genial as a stove, and Wren gives him back only that it's what's in the book and she's the hands, not the stamp.

Coombs turns the same offer on Miko when she drifts in off the ore stub, and Miko, fanning her three bought names and three coast tickets, does the arithmetic out loud — paper names don't buy meals and a green board only means the trains run — and for once asks him a real question about the wage instead of a lie.

At the ore stub Kass opens the tender's belly with Doan and finds it carries no transponder and posts to no master board, and under the floor the same blank mount and cut harness as the four rigs that vanished off Kettering — one of a fleet that lives off every book.

Wren stops reciting 36.4 and asks Rhea for the one thing running can't give her: to be taken to the man she counted while he's still breathing — the machine-truster now the one who has to weigh a face against a plate.

Rhea walks Wren the two paces to the back-room door with the cathode light bleeding under it, while Coombs fills the shop behind them to say the tender's warm and the desk's clock is running — whoever walks back out of that room is who rolls at the bell.
events: Teodoro read the morning desk's hold order aloud — Wren remanded to the coast with the collecting tender already logged, File 2244's physical recovery for Marlowe due at the shift bell, and Anza's green chain holding only if she's surrendered — and the plate's countersign field came up already filled with Marlowe's badge.
Coombs offered Wren a warm bunk, a logged wage and the permanent erasure of her proof, and she refused to be bought, telling him to take her on the book's line as the hands and not the stamp.

Coombs offers Miko the warm logged bunk, Miko does the arithmetic out loud — three bought names buy no meals and a green board only means the trains run — and asks him plainly who pays her wage, learning it comes out of Anza's own hundred-and-ten ration-day line, then asks what it costs him if she walks at the Weir and watches him strip off a glove.

Kass and Doan inspect Coombs's tender at the ore stub and discover it has no transponder, a factory-blank mount, and a cleanly cut harness identical to the four ghost rigs that vanished from Kettering's master board — confirming a fleet of unlogged rigs operating off every book.

Wren stops her count and asks Rhea to walk her to Marlowe and vouch with her own eyes rather than the plate, while Coombs warns that a stale voice line means the officer with the hat comes instead and Rhea hands Ivo's cartridge watch to Nour.
